rows.title: CarPlay / Bluetooth narration
rows.test: Reran audio-session handoff, transport and scene-brief checks in the full gate.
rows.result: Automated checks pass. No iPhone 12 Pro Max or actual CarPlay route was available; the reported stutter is not verified fixed.
rows.next: On the same car route, compare a native-voice turn with synthesized speech, then wired versus wireless CarPlay. Capture read-route diagnostics. Direct Bluetooth is the tracker’s demonstrated workaround. There is not enough evidence here to prescribe a new engine fix.

rows.title: Companion flaws and earned growth
rows.test: Reran on-screen growth, off-screen refusal, wrong/unchanged flaw rejection, speaker aliases and companion-impulse cadence.
rows.result: All tested rules pass. Valid tags update the flaw and retain history. This proves the route works, not that the GM chooses earned growth in real play.
rows.next: Keep the existing single impulse channel. Judge a filing after a genuine defining moment; do not add another scheduler or prompt without a reproduced failure.

rows.title: Spoken pause and resume
rows.test: Reran exact utterances and hold/resume dispatch, including ordinary-sentence negatives and bare continue.
rows.result: Vocabulary and dispatch pass; executor wiring is source-checked. No real microphone, steering-wheel control or car session was exercised.
rows.next: While parked, say pause with the mic open, verify it stays held across a turn, then exercise the supported resume/tap route. Native recognition normally opens after narration, so narrator interruption needs its own real-route check.

rows.title: Present resident personality
rows.test: Reran present/absent/party roster fixtures for trait, flaw, appearance and motivation, including stable-prompt isolation.
rows.result: The serving fix passes. It cannot turn a sheet and memory describing a guarded, polite vendor into the feral character the owner remembers.
rows.next: Review the intended sheet/persona, export from the source campaign and refresh the Village. Contradictory historical Village memory needs the existing reviewed resident-reset path on a copy. Avoid a special-case Nyla prompt.

rows.title: Motivation retirement and rebirth
rows.test: Reran settlement, birth, retained history, on-screen guards, paperwork rejection, fallback, prompt and sheet cases.
rows.result: Pass: settlement empties the standing field, keeps history and serves none standing. A new purpose uses the same lifecycle helpers. Story appropriateness remains a play judgement.
rows.next: In play, verify the settlement toast and sheet, then that a new purpose comes from the story. Keep one lifecycle; #515 checks the summary fallback regression.

rows.title: Portable persona
rows.test: Reran five persona groups. Independently exported Nyla through portableSheet from an in-memory copy of Village Ammut t279 and compared selected lines with named-speaker extraction.
rows.result: Five lines captured, all from that speaker’s extraction. Source save stayed byte-identical. Tests cover other-speaker exclusion, sparse-history retention, hero exclusion and presence-gated serving. A real server-library round-trip and resulting dialogue were not tested.
rows.next: Export a known character from the source campaign, inspect Voice lines/Manner, refresh the destination and judge the next dialogue. Keep the shared capture and renderer unless that play check reveals a failure.

rows.title: Audio envelope editor
rows.test: Drove Chrome: drag point, exact time, add/remove, shape selection, play/stop, WAV download, invalid preset, 390 px viewport and a different recording.
rows.result: Passed. WAV was 123,346 bytes with a silent final sample. Phone screenshot is readable with no horizontal overflow. Screenshots were visually inspected.
rows.next: No defect reproduced. Interaction/export works; this is not a new subjective listening judgement of every curve.

rows.title: Alchemist entrance bell
rows.test: On final v1.1141, loaded the copied t279 scene: load is silent; entrance rings once; repeated commits do not ring; pause/exit cut it; resume does not replay; re-entry rings once.
rows.result: Passed with no page errors. Reran after another session’s bell-volume update. Playback-state checks cannot judge final loudness on the owner’s device.
rows.next: Listen to the final v1.1141 mix alongside narration at normal ambience volume. No code defect was reproduced.

rows.title: Alchemist bubbling and glass
rows.test: Loaded the actual covered/interior t279 alchemist scene in isolated Chrome; checked correct bed, decoded glass accent and no page errors. Also ran ambience transition/control scripts.
rows.result: Passed. The original covered-versus-sealed mismatch no longer selects the hearth. Owner approval of the calmer mix is historical tracker evidence, not a fresh listening claim.
rows.next: No new defect reproduced. Local Chromium selection/playback passes; deployment cache and iOS listening remain outside this pass.

rows.title: Duplicate prompt facts
rows.test: Reran both duplication groups: one hero bond, preserved NPC/bond-less edges, Village location residue and unchanged adventure list. Captured actual Village t279 prompt.
rows.result: Passed. Current prompt: 58,638 stable characters, 66,507 volatile characters. Receipt includes graph and location lines. The earlier 762-character saving was not independently remeasured against old code.
rows.next: Keep one rendering location per fact and the omission guards. No further abstraction is needed.

rows.title: Ten browser scripts without Playwright
rows.test: Ran shop, stash, ways, ambient, reload, transitions, audio cache, general audio, hearth and noctina using system Chrome.
rows.result: All ten pass. First cache run failed because my temporary server did not map / to index.html. After correcting that route, the unchanged project script passed, including offline reload.
rows.next: Keep the shared cdp-browser driver. No dependency install or separate driver per script is needed.

rows.title: Trade tags before arrival
rows.test: Tested [WARES:Brass comb|3 gp|Frizwick][SUBLOCATION:The Iron Cauldron][LOCATION:The Village], plus prose boundaries and wanted/keeper/item/coin regressions.
rows.result: Passed: comb files on the Cauldron, not the old shop; sublocation remains The Iron Cauldron. Description tags retain their separate chronological rule.
rows.next: Older still-open paragraphs predate the built fix. Use the existing block-aware lookup, not another place sequencer.

rows.title: Town description filed on destination
rows.test: Tested LOCATION_DESC before and after a move, and write-once behavior.
rows.result: Passed: before-move description files on the town; bathhouse remains undescribed. After-move description targets the destination.
rows.next: The fix prevents new damage. Historical Runelords descriptions still require the existing map cleanup tool on a copied save. This pass did not repair them.

rows.title: Summary invents a second motivation
rows.test: Reran tagged standing purpose followed by a paraphrased summary, filler on empty purpose, and Done running versus Done: / fulfilled.
rows.result: Pass: standing purpose remains, filler is dropped and Done running does not settle it.
rows.next: Keep the summary as a fallback to the same helpers, not a second authority.

rows.title: Counted transfers and same-name collisions
rows.test: Tested forward quantity limits, empty reverse transfers, gift at home with a matching chest item, and independent loot beside a companion throw.
rows.result: Counts and chest cases pass. Still broken: “You loot a dagger. [ITEM_GAINED:Dagger] Bram throws his dagger. [COMPANION_ITEM_LOST:Bram|Dagger]” ends with an empty hero pack and an earlier +Dagger receipt.
rows.next: Cause: tag_table.js consumes matching igHits across the whole reply and rolls back the hero’s gain without proving a transfer. Use one explicit {from,to,item,qty} transfer and commit both sides together. Until that path exists, never reconcile across intervening prose merely by name. Same-block ambiguity should refuse visibly. Preserve the passing quantity caps.

rows.title: Teacher or adjective steals a hero ability
rows.test: Reran Daeris showed/gave/teaches, Sable cloak and Will saves, actual third-person companion abilities and hero/you guards.
rows.result: Pass: reported teaching/common-word cases stay on the hero; recognized companion subjects still route.
rows.next: Keep the decision in one subject resolver. These tested language shapes do not prove every possible English sentence.

rows.title: Plain companion departures
rows.test: Reran six departure positives and five object/body-side negatives: left., left without a word, left at dawn, just left, had already left.
rows.result: Pass: plain departures count; left her side, left hand and object-bearing negatives remain protected.
rows.next: Keep the one clause recognizer and paired positive/negative fixtures.

rows.title: Unused definitions
rows.test: Ran tokenizer self-test and current tracked-file census, plus full gate.
rows.result: Four tokenizer checks pass. Census: 3,969 line-start declarations, 655 scanned files, none dead. Named removed definitions are absent.
rows.next: No further deletion indicated. This is a conservative token census with strings retained, not a whole-program reachability proof.

rows.title: Expected refusals sent as crash reports
rows.test: Reran W2/summary-identity refusal strikes 1/2/3 and ordinary extraction failures; source-checked summarize catch wiring.
rows.result: Pass: strikes 1/2 suppress mail; quarantine strike 3 reports; other extraction failures report immediately. No webhook/email was sent and production reports were not sampled.
rows.next: Keep one reporting decision at the boundary. Confirm fewer duplicate reports on the next real refusal; this pass does not claim end-to-end delivery.

rows.title: Repaired-map arrival points at a twin
rows.test: Reran a node whose old key prefix differs from its current parent: arrival pointer, visit, item, state note and geo list.
rows.result: Pass: composed world/leaf alias resolves to the real node; no twin is created. Included after correctly parsing code-span pipes in its status.
rows.next: Keep existing alias registration. No per-consumer special-case lookup is needed.

rows.title: Voice continuity across sheet replacement
rows.test: Reran five groups: hero/companion adoption, missing versus explicit library fields, changed-gender casting and fallen-companion rejoin including clears.
rows.result: All five pass structurally. No synthesized before/after line from a live replacement was heard. The tracker’s separate review requirement is not fulfilled by this pass.
rows.next: Replace a voiced companion and listen to the next line. Keep the shared voice-field helpers, rather than new provider-specific branches.

rows.title: Merge studio missing script
rows.test: Opened actual studio in Chrome, loaded two distinct synthetic records, ran runApply, checked mandatory verification and merged download.
rows.result: Pass: 30 manifest files load; two records become one; verified result and download appear; no page errors. No transcript/RAG excerpts exist in this fixture, so its RAG probe is explicitly vacuous.
rows.next: Missing-script failure is resolved. Keep the canonical manifest; do not interpret this as RAG coverage.

rows.title: Place sequencing across a reply
rows.test: Reran A4 plus current #511 block semantics, #512 descriptions and #529 repaired-map arrival.
rows.result: All tested cases pass. Earlier blockers #511 and #529 have passing current-build tests. Trade tags use their block arrival; descriptions use their own text position.
rows.next: No remaining failure reproduced in these fixtures. Keep one timeline with the deliberate tag-boundary lookup rules.

rows.title: Car Mode undo loses a stowed item
rows.test: Tested ordinary undo, swapped-away hero, switching back, grouped moves, expiry/busy refusal and unpaired story placement.
rows.result: Pass: hero swap refuses without losing spear; switching back restores it. Unpaired placement returns pack:false and says off the record here / nobody’s pack held it; it no longer says back with you.
rows.next: Initial independent expectation was stale: #597 deliberately permits record-only undo. Corrected assertion checks that contract and the honest sentence. No reported code failure remains.

rows.title: Chest quantities and identity
rows.test: Reran D2 counted take, plural/dash normalization and legacy healing; retested transfers and counted wares.
rows.result: Original chest copy-machine cases pass. Broader conservation still fails: Arrow x20 purchase yields Arrow x39; independent same-name loot can be rolled back by a companion’s failed throw.
rows.next: Normalize a ware once to {baseName,qty,priceCp,pricePer}. Add bare Arrow twenty times, never a counted label twenty times. Use the explicit transfer boundary in #518 for cross-owner movement.

rows.title: Large and companion quantities
rows.test: Reran x12/x10 hero changes, Torch x3/x2 companion changes, one-line stack trade, empty reverse transfer and gift at home.
rows.result: Quantity grammar and newly bounded transfers pass. Broader hold remains justified by #518’s Dagger collision: correct arithmetic cannot rescue incorrectly paired actions.
rows.next: Keep the shared quantity grammar. Fix transfer association once, without adding per-handler quantity exceptions.

rows.title: One wanted offer pays repeatedly
rows.test: Tested ordinary retirement, expiry and no-payment discard, then three decorated names matching one Warded ring want in the planner and actual browser clicks.
rows.result: Failed: one 40 gp offer paid 120 gp. Every row receives its own one-item allowance and the whole plan is priced before shared-want retirement. Also inherits #591’s unrelated-coin failure.
rows.next: One remaining quantity per wanted offer must govern the whole plan. Each matching row consumes the same allowance; reject extra unpriced units or use their independent ordinary value with an explicit receipt. Retire only from an accepted paid-sale line.

rows.title: Silver, copper and price units
rows.test: Tested plural coppers, mixed sale/buy, 20 for 1 gp, 5 gp per dozen, 1 gp 5 sp, counter prices and counted ware through WARES/shopTradeApply.
rows.result: Copper/parser checks pass: -3 coppers subtracts 3 cp; two 30 cp sales against a 100 cp buy cost 40 cp. Bundle/compound forms parse. Arrow x20 still yields 39 arrows for a twenty-arrow charge.
rows.next: Keep copper accounting and one coin parser. Fix name/count normalization as in #575. A non-divisible bundle’s displayed unit price rounds, while its plan uses the bundle share; that is distinct from the reproduced item-count defect.

rows.title: Library refresh replays stash twice
rows.test: Reran ordinary and already-exported-mark cases. Stowed one of five Blasting charges, exported the four-charge sheet, changed the in-memory campaign ID, then refreshed that same sheet.
rows.result: Failed: four charges become three. stashMarkKey uses campId, so the carried mark under the old ID is missed and the existing move replays. Same-ID refresh passes.
rows.next: Use a stable stash-journal origin key that survives campaign rekey/import, and the same key on sheet marks. Migrate the old mark once. Never replay from zero just because a storage ID changed. Add a real import/rekey round-trip regression before shipping; this probe isolates the boundary in memory.

rows.title: Client/server slug mismatch
rows.test: Full gate ran shared slug/hash tests: (Ammut) → ammut, Åsa Lindé → sa_lind; both client call sites delegate; blueprint trimming/length remain pinned.
rows.result: Client checks pass. No fresh deployed-server connection or authenticated Replace/Update was performed. Historical deployment receipt is not a new live check.
rows.next: Check a punctuation-edged character name against the deployed library. Keep one shared implementation and vendoring hash; no new slug rule is needed.

rows.title: Discard retires wanted offer
rows.test: Original no-coin discard passes. Added: Frizwick returns 1 cp change, then hero discards a wanted 40 gp ring in the same reply.
rows.result: Failed: +1 cp, ring removed, wanted list empty, receipt Want met. R.goldIn > 0 means some money arrived; it does not mean this item was sold.
rows.next: Retire only from an identified completed sale: offer, item, quantity, payment. The counter already has this boundary. If GM tags cannot prove the association, keep the want and surface uncertainty. Another discard-word exception would be fragile.

rows.title: Counter QA assumes two wanted units
rows.test: Ran real counter QA: one 3 sp wanted whistle, second tap clears selection, and silver/copper prices for ration/cake/arrows.
rows.result: Pass: first click enables Complete at +3 sp; second clears and disables it. Rations show 2 sp 5 cp. Screenshots generated.
rows.next: The harness matches the current rule. Its green result does not cover several decorated rows sharing one want; #577 reproduces that separate defect.

rows.title: Designer clips at 800 characters
rows.test: Ran actual Designer with exact 836-character magistrate text: full load/breakout, sentence revision, original retention, failed/late revision, draft reload and automatic Apply. Full gate runs seven pure revision checks.
rows.result: Pass: original ends safe-passage promise.; revision ends safe passage. Both renders visually inspected. Invalid/late output preserves original/newer text. Model responses were fixtures, not a live quality evaluation.
rows.next: Keep lossless authoring and one explicit revision pass, with original retained and runtime bounds unchanged. No clipping reproduced.
